_comment: What the live TTN decoder must produce from bytes the encoder actually emitted.
Case names come from tools/emit_vectors.cpp; scripts/check_golden_vectors.py fails if
the two lists disagree, so a new case cannot be added on one side only.
These numbers are written from the decoder's documented behavior, not copied from its
output. Copying the output would make the test agree with whatever the decoder does,

all_fields._why: Every field the node can report, at a data rate that fits all of them.

slowest_rate._why: Eleven bytes is all the network allows at its slowest rate. These three fields are the ones worth keeping: whether the node is dying, and the two readings the station exists to take.

weather_only._why: The pack is silent. Its fields are absent rather than zero, so nobody downstream can mistake a dead sensor for a flat battery.

pack_only._why: The weather station is silent, and the same rule applies in the other direction.

nothing_valid._why: Both sensors silent. The encoder produces no bytes at all, and the node sends nothing.
